signal: leanblueprint ... uses{...} annotations generate the dependency graph and the lean{...}/leanok links track formalization status per node
why: The reference states the blueprint-node practice: a node is a human-readable outline entry with declared dependencies and a Lean link tracking its formalization status, stated before it is proved, with the working node-size criterion that one contributor can complete one node without global context.

signal: The extraction ladder: 1. A sub-argument repeats within one proof -> name it as a local have. 2. The statement is independently interesting, or extraction sheds hypotheses -> standalone lemma. 3. The proof reads as long and unwieldy -> split it.
why: The ladder gives the decision rule for lifting part of a proof out: a repeated sub-argument first becomes a local have, then a standalone lemma once its statement is independently interesting or drops unneeded hypotheses; the worked min_comm example turns a quantified have into a lemma used twice and closes both directions with le_antisymm.

signal: Write one tactic, check diagnostics (use `done` to see unsolved goals), repeat. Never write multiple tactics before checking; `done` is required when expecting next steps
why: The core proof-writing loop of the skill: after every tactic the agent checks diagnostics, with `done` as the check that goals remain, before writing the next tactic. It is a process rule about how to advance a proof, applied again at lines 17-25 (error priority) and 57-62 (cleanup), rather than a tactic recipe.

signal: before: theorem main_theorem : A = C := by sorry; after: lemma1 : A = B := by sorry; lemma2 : B = C := by sorry; main_theorem := by rw [lemma1, lemma2]
why: Lemma-splitting decomposition, which the move vocabulary does not name: one hard theorem is replaced by two helper lemmas plus a rewrite skeleton that composes them, so each remaining hole is smaller than the original. The skill frames it as moving sorries earlier in the file (go to the target theorem first), and the rewrite chain rw [lemma1, lemma2] is the whole parent proof.

signal: match n with | 0 => sorry -- fill in later | 1 => sorry -- fill in later | n + 2 => -- WORK ON THIS FIRST
why: The rule places holes deliberately on the easy branches and works the hardest branch first, stating the reason: if the hard case fails, effort on easy cases is wasted. The site is the work-ordering use of sorry holes within a case split.

signal: The Solution: Generalize First, Instantiate Last; suffices ∀ s, statement_about s by ... convert this ?_ <;> exact h_specific; intro s
why: For the rewriting failure motive is not type correct, the skill proves the statement for an arbitrary parameter and instantiates at the end with convert, so the dependent term is never abstracted over. Six lines state the failure mode and the generalized proof shape.

signal: calc |f ω - h ω| _ = ... := by ring_nf _ ≤ ... := abs_add; calc (m:ℝ)⁻¹ * |∑ k, f k| _ ≤ ... := by gcongr; three chains, one lemma per step
why: Three worked calc chains (triangle inequality, sum bound, gcongr-in-calc) show the move: one step per line, each step closed by a single lemma or tactic, the `_` continuation carrying the previous right-hand side, with the stated rule to start the chain from the goal state after simp rather than the expected form.

signal: New definitions should come with associated lemmas and appropriate attributes (`@[simp]`, `@[ext]`, etc.); Needing `erw`, or `rfl` after `simp`/`rw` usually means the API is missing lemmas
why: The review rule is the API-lemma discipline: every definition ships the lemmas that let clients use it without unfolding, tagged for simp/ext. The second bullet turns a proof smell, erw or rfl after simp/rw, into the diagnosis that an interface lemma is missing.

signal: rcases Nat.even_or_odd n with h | h; one branch per case; obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h; use ...; ring
why: A closed proof of 2 ∣ n * (n + 1) that splits on the finite disjunction even/odd, one branch per case, each branch naming its witness and closing with ring; exhaustiveness comes from Nat.even_or_odd. No sorry.

signal: #guard_msgs in example : ... := by some_tactic; lake env lean YourFile.lean; lake exe minimize YourFile.lean
why: Three-step isolation workflow: capture the exact error with #guard_msgs in a test file, confirm the guard reproduces it with lake env lean, then shrink the file with the minimizer. Each step checks the previous one, and the later checklist (lines 103-108) requires the output to compile with the expected error.

signal: let mW : MeasurableSpace Ω := MeasurableSpace.comap W mγ; let mZW := ...; have hmW_le : mW ≤ mΩ := hW.comap_le; have hmZW_le ...; have hmW_le_mZW ...
why: The proof introduces two named objects with let (mW and mZW), then discharges their properties in named haves before a one-line trivial; the names are what the rest of the proof refers to instead of restating the comap terms. Closed, no sorry.

signal: have hk_bound : ∀ i : Fin (m' + 1), k i < n := by ... omega  ->  private lemma strictMono_all_lt_succ_last {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (hk : StrictMono k) ...
why: Before/after of lifting an embedded have into a top-level private lemma: the surrounding context (m', k, hk_mono) becomes explicit parameters and the proof body is copied, so the main proof calls the helper; both versions close (omega before, apply/exact after).

signal: Type 4: Complex structural proof -> Break into sub-sorries with clear strategy; Type 5: Actually needs new lemma -> Extract as helper lemma, prove separately
why: The reference classifies why a hole resists filling and gives the sorrify response for the structural case: replace the too-large goal with sub-sorries and work them one at a time (Type 4), escalating to a separate helper lemma when the hole is a missing statement (Type 5).

signal: Actions: 1 Audit ... 2 Search ... 3 Plan ... 4 Approval ... 5 Apply ... 6 Verify ... 7 Report; Helper scope defaults: single use -> have, reused in file -> private theorem, public only with approval
why: A harness command specifying the process for strategy-level proof change: audit for long proofs and thin definition APIs, search mathlib, plan with measured impact, approve per batch, apply behind a diagnostic gate (revert on sorry increase), then report; it also fixes the helper-scope rule (local have vs private theorem).

signal: have idem (x : G) : (x ◇ x) ◇ (x ◇ x) = (x ◇ x) := by repeat rw [← h]; have comm ...; have op_idem ...; exact fun _ _ ↦ by rw [← op_idem, comm, op_idem]
why: Theorem Equation387_implies_Equation43 does not rewrite the hypothesis directly: it first proves three auxiliary laws that carry the idea - idempotence of x ◇ x (idem), that x ◇ x commutes with y (comm), and that (x ◇ x) ◇ (y ◇ y) = x ◇ y (op_idem) - and the final two-line commutativity proof is just rw with these three named facts. The hypotheses are exactly what the blueprint node 387_implies_43 establishes in prose (blueprint/src/chapter/implications.tex:5-27).

signal: use (g a (pow5 a))  rw [f, h4, h3, ← h]
why: Eq1689.lem_fixf proves forall a, exists b, f a b = a by naming the candidate: four have-facts h1-h4 (built from lem_1 and lem_2) establish the properties of g a (pow5 a), use introduces that term as the witness, and a single rw closes f a (g a (pow5 a)) = a. The lemma then supplies the hypothesis of lem_fixf_implies_eq2 in Equation1689_implies_Equation2 (Subgraph.lean:330-333).

signal: induction m generalizing acc | have h (m acc) : @toListTR.go α acc m = toList m ++ acc | simpa using (h m []).symm
why: toList_eq_toListTR must show @toList = @toListTR. After funext it proves the stronger statement h, quantified over every accumulator acc, by induction on m generalizing acc, and reaches the stated goal only at the end by instantiating acc := [] (simpa using (h m []).symm). The generalised form is what makes the Fork case go through.

signal: obtain ((heq | hsub | hsub) | hnf) := hproj.proj_or_nf (bu rw x ⋆ bu rw y)
why: bu_nf inducts on x; in the Fork case the IsProjOrNF hypothesis yields only a disjunction, which the proof destructs into four exhaustive branches - equality heq, left subterm, right subterm, already-normal hnf - and discharges each (the subterm branches via everywhere_of_subterm_of_everywhere). The exhaustiveness of this case analysis is the whole Fork obligation, and every branch closes.

signal: f.comp f₁ = f.comp f₂ ↔ f₁ = f₂ := ⟨MagmaHom.ext ∘ hf.forall.2 ∘ DFunLike.ext_iff.1, (· ▸ rfl)⟩
why: MagmaHom.cancel_right proves an iff by supplying both directions in one anonymous constructor: the forward direction cancels the surjective f on the right (pointwise equality via hf.forall, then equality of homomorphisms by MagmaHom.ext), and the backward direction transports along the assumed equality. Each direction of the equivalence is its own proof obligation, discharged separately.
